study type: Propensity score-matched analysis of a retrospective cohort study
cohort: 768 healthy pregnant women with viable, vertex singleton pregnancies at 37 to 40 weeks of gestation
finding: Elective induction of labor at term was not associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery in low-risk pregnancies, but there was a higher incidence of NICU admission at 38 weeks of gestation in the elective induction group compared to the expectant management group.
